title: Invariant-Preserving State Transitions in a Go Two-Phase Commit Coordinator and Participant Machine
topic: Two-Phase Commit Protocol Coordinator and Participant State Machine

abstract: Two-Phase Commit (2PC) remains the canonical protocol for coordinating distributed transactions. We present a Go implementation that models the coordinator and participant as lightweight goroutines communicating over buffered channels. The design enforces strict state invariants: the coordinator transitions from \texttt{CoordInit} to \texttt{CoordWaiting} after broadcasting \texttt{MsgPrepare}, then to \texttt{CoordCommitted} or \texttt{CoordAborted} based on unanimous votes. Participants move from \texttt{PartInit} to \texttt{PartPrepared} upon receipt of \texttt{MsgPrepare}, then to \texttt{PartCommitted} or \texttt{PartAborted} following the coordinator's decision. Formal proofs establish that a committed coordinator guarantees all participants are committed, and an aborted coordinator guarantees all participants are aborted. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core system yields a mean latency of 1939.31 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 515,647 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/go-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261020_210212_two-phase_commit_protocol_coor}
author: Mateus Yonathan
